plot: The afternoon after Bertha's new glasses, the little car on the hill is Bolt's niece Nell, who says the hill top 'sings hooo' by itself; Bolt brushes it off as the wind and Nell feels nobody listens to small cars, but she and Pip notice the sound only comes when leaves fly sideways (Grumpy mentioned early he dropped Benny's old bottles up there), Turbo's zooming wind makes it sing two notes, and when the wind stops Bolt finally listens and asks what is new on the hill: Grumpy's crate of empty milk bottles, which whistle like a flute in the wind; Bolt says sorry, gives Nell his hat as 'Detective Nell', the hill plays a sunset song, and Nell's mum brings news they might move to Wheelburg.

script.title: The Autumn Hill Is Singing!
script.description: Bolt's niece Nell hears Wheelburg Hill sing. Inspector Bolt #38

set.place: the top of Wheelburg Hill with the old wooden fence, a bench and the view over town, a breezy autumn afternoon until sunset

beats.say: Uncle Bolt! Uncle Bolt! Come quick! The hill is singing!
Up there, by the old fence! It goes hooo, all by itself!
Nell?! My little niece? What are you doing in Wheelburg?
It was the afternoon after Bertha got her new glasses.
The car on the hill was Nell. Bolt's niece, visiting.
Mum's buying buns at Benny's bakery. I drove up for the view!
Then, hooo! A big sound! And nobody was there!
Hills don't sing, Nell. It's just the wind. Let's get a bun.
But I heard it! I'm being a detective. Like you.
Bolt smiled. But he wasn't really listening.
Now THAT... is not only the wind.
Bolt! Did you hear that? The whole hill went hooo!
I heard it first! I'm Nell. I'm a detective.
A detective? Me too! Well, a helper. I'm Pip!
Two small cars. One big mystery. Friends in one second.
Careful, you two. Sounds can travel from far away.
Then let's find where it comes from! Engines off. Ears on!
Everyone turned off their engines. The hill went very, very quiet.
Why is everybody so quiet up here? Is it nap time?
Shh, Grumpy! We're listening to the hill!
Hm. I was up here this morning. Dropped off Benny's old bottles.
Nothing sang for me. Nothing ever sings for me.
Look! Look at the leaves! They're flying sideways!
A puff of wind blew across the hill top. Red leaves flew.
See? Wind, then hooo. No wind, no hooo!
The sound only comes with the wind. That's a real clue.
A real clue? From me?
From you. But wind needs something to sing through.
Pip, if we solve this, Uncle Bolt will take me seriously!
Then let's follow the hooo! Small cars are good listeners!
Hello up there! I saw you all the way from town!
New glasses! I can see every car on this hill!
Hello, Big Bertha! Did you hear the hill sing?
Sing? Oh! I thought that was Grumpy humming.
I don't hum. I have never hummed.
Whoa! Everyone's up here? Is there a race? Can I come?
No race. A mystery! The hill sings when the wind blows!
Wind? I can MAKE wind! Watch this!
Turbo zoomed round and round the hill top. Leaves flew everywhere.
It sang louder! And it sang two songs at once!
Two notes. One high, one low. So it's not one thing.
Many little things... singing together!
The two small detectives rolled slowly along the old wooden fence.
It's louder here. Much louder. Right by the bench!
But there's nothing here. Only leaves and an old crate.
Then the wind stopped. And the hill went quiet again.
No! If the wind stops, we lose our only clue!
And everyone will say we made it up!
This time, Bolt rolled over. And this time, he listened.
Nell, what is up here today that wasn't here yesterday?
I wasn't here yesterday, Uncle Bolt. I only came today!
I was. Only one new thing up here. My crate.
Nobody had looked at the old crate at all. Not even Bolt.
Grumpy, what's inside your crate?
Benny's old milk bottles. Empty. For the glass truck.
Empty bottles! Uncle Bolt, I know! I KNOW!
When you blow over a bottle, it goes hooo! Like a flute!
That's true. Wind over an empty bottle top makes a sound.
Big bottles sing low. Small bottles sing high.
The wind blew. The bottles sang. And the hill got the blame.
So something did sing for me after all. Huh.
And my zooming made it sing louder! I'm a wind maker!
No singing hill. Just a singing crate. How lovely!
Nell, I'm sorry. I said hills don't sing. I didn't listen.
That's okay, Uncle Bolt. You listened in the end.
Small detectives ask big questions. They always deserve an answer.
Then Bolt did something he never does. He gave Nell his hat.
Detective Nell. Case closed. Just for today.
Detective Nell! Pip, did you hear that?!
Can we play the bottles? Turbo, make more wind!
So Turbo zoomed past the crate, again and again.
And the whole hill sang a sunset song for Nell.
Then Nell's mum drove up with warm buns. And big news.
Uncle Bolt... Mum says we might come to live in Wheelburg!
Live here? In Wheelburg? Next to me?
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
